svg.title: Four Gates Before an Equipment File Goes Out
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-equipment-approval-gates; chapter number: 5; chart type: decision_tree; title: Four Gates Before an Equipment File Goes Out; subtitle: Collateral, vendor, credit, and payment checks; caption: The machine secures its own deal, so the asset, the vendor, the borrower's credit and the payment math each get screened before submission.; assumptions note: Gate order is an operating sequence assembled from separate practitioners; thresholds are as each speaker stated them.; note: Sources are ION Capital - Loan Broker University, The Banking Podcast, ROK Financial with Ryan Vehey, Joe Camberato, and BizMoney Explained.; nodes: gate: G1; question: Can the lender resell every listed asset, with no existing UCC filing on the equipment?; pass next: G2; fail action: Stop; lenders will not take second position on an asset and want recent units they can resell.; gate: G2; question: Are the seller and the invoice price verified as a real vendor sale?; pass next: G3; fail action: Fix before submission; underwriters catch the friend-down-the-street invoice every time.; gate: G3; question: Does credit fit the program, such as 620-plus for application-only leases to about $150,000, or 700-plus with comparable past debt for startups?; pass next: G4; fail action: Screen out very high revolving utilization, active collections and auction-house purchases; push files under 50 percent utilization.; gate: G4; question: Does the payment survive weak demand, where $900 of incremental cash against a $1,500 payment leaves a $600 monthly shortfall?; pass next: Submit to the matched lender; fail action: Restructure the term or walk away.

text.title: Four Gates Before an Equipment File Goes Out
text.tspan: Four Gates Before an Equipment File Goes Out

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Can the lender resell every listed asset, with no existing UCC filing on the equipment?; pass next: G2; fail action: Stop; lenders will not take second position on an asset and want recent units they can resell.

gate: G2; question: Are the seller and the invoice price verified as a real vendor sale?; pass next: G3; fail action: Fix before submission; underwriters catch the friend-down-the-street invoice every time.

gate: G3; question: Does credit fit the program, such as 620-plus for application-only leases to about $150,000, or 700-plus with comparable past debt for startups?; pass next: G4; fail action: Screen out very high revolving utilization, active collections and auction-house purchases; push files under 50 percent utilization.

gate: G4; question: Does the payment survive weak demand, where $900 of incremental cash against a $1,500 payment leaves a $600 monthly shortfall?; pass next: Submit to the matched lender; fail action: Restructure the term or walk away.

text.title: Assumptions: Gate order is an operating sequence assembled from separate practitioners; thresholds are as each speaker stated them.
text.tspan: Assumptions: Gate order is an operating sequence assembled from separate practitioners; thresholds are as each speaker stated them.

text.title: No relationships supplied; nodes shown as an unconnected register. Connectors encode supplied relationships; node positions are schematic.
